name: lib/chaos
title: chaos
summary: Seeded, scheduled fault injection that cannot run in production. ChaosEngine decides, per invocation, whether an operation gets a fault (error, latency, timeout, drop, truncate, malformed); it is the FaultInjector the N5 resilience pipeline takes.

enabled.rule: Off: decide() returns null without drawing; the n2 wrappers run the function untouched and validate nothing.

seed.rule: mulberry32 seed. The n2 wrappers (withChaos, chaosMiddleware, chaosWrap) use a random seed when none is given, as they used Math.random before.

faults.rule: In order; each rate in [0, 1]; rates sum to at most 1 (1e-9 tolerance). latency carries integer minMs <= maxMs.

schedule.rule: Entry i is invocation i's decision. Used up first; a schedule entry draws nothing from the generator.

environment.rule: production or prod (any case) forbids enabled chaos.

errorRate, latencyMs.rule: When faults is absent: faults = [{error, rate: errorRate}, {latency, rate: 1 - errorRate, minMs, maxMs}]. Giving faults and either of these is a config error.

behaviour: decide(): if disabled → null. If production now → null (checked on every call). If a schedule entry remains → it. Else u = nextU32(); walk faults in order with cumulative thresholds floor(cumRate * 2^32), capped at 2^32 so a cumulative rate of 1 always fires; the first with u < threshold wins. latency draws once more: ms = minMs + nextU32() % (maxMs - minMs + 1). No fault, no second draw.
mulberry32 is the spec's exact generator (state += 0x6D2B79F5; imul mixing); the same seed gives the same decisions in every build.

applyFault (TS): error and drop reject ChaosError without running the operation; latency waits then runs; timeout never settles until the signal aborts; truncate halves a string (by code point), array, Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer, else hands the value to mutate or rejects ChaosError{kind: truncate}; malformed replaces the result with mutate's output or the marker {"mzizi-chaos":.
Rust is sans-IO: the host applies the decision (waits, drops the future, truncates with truncate_str / truncate_slice).

productionGuard.rule: Hard, no override. Enabling chaos where the environment is production fails at construction with ChaosForbiddenError (code chaos-forbidden), before the rest of the config is read.
productionGuard.ts: Production when environment is production/prod, or process.env.NODE_ENV === "production", or import.meta.env.PROD === true. An explicit non-production environment does not override the other two.
productionGuard.rs: Production when the host passes Environment::Production, or passes no environment and this is a release build (cfg!(not(debug_assertions))). A host that runs chaos in an optimised staging build passes a non-production Environment.
throws: new ChaosEngine / createChaos with enabled: true in production
withChaos(fn, { enabled: true, ... }) in production: the returned promise rejects, fn is not called
chaosMiddleware({ enabled: true, ... }) and chaosWrap(fn, { enabled: true, ... }) in production: at creation
productionGuard.allowed: enabled: false in production: no error, nothing injected, fn runs untouched.

errors.name: ChaosError
errors.when: An injected error, drop or untruncatable truncate. TS keeps injected: true and chaosType (= kind).

errors.name: ResilienceConfigError
errors.when: Invalid config (TS: a RangeError subclass; Rust: ConfigError inside ChaosBuildError::Config).

covenant: Injection is logged under [mzizi:chaos] with the fault kind (and latency ms) only.
gaps: The fault interface (Fault, FaultInjector, mulberry32) is defined here until the N5 core (mzizi-resilience) lands; then it is imported from there.
mzizi-chaos (the blast-radius diagnostics) still draws Math.random for its own injection helpers; moving it onto ChaosEngine is a follow-up.
